text: .1760 Eseridine Salicylate, Rabeprazole, p.1765 p.1729 Ranitidine Bismuth Esomeprazole, p.1729 Citrate, p.1768 Famotidine, p.1730 Ranitidine, p.1766 Lafutidine, p.1739 Revaprazan, p.1768 Lansoprazole, p.1739 Roxatidine, p.1769 Niperotidine, p.1751 Urogastrone, p.1778 Nizatidine, p.1751 Antispasmodics Antispasmodics are drugs used for their relaxant action on smooth muscle, either direct or through an antimuscarinic action on the parasympathetic innervation. They play a role in the management of gastrointestinal spasm and irri- table bowel syndrome (below) as well as other disorders associated with smooth muscle spasm. Those described in this chapter are mainly antimuscarinics; drugs in other chapters that may be used for relaxation of smooth muscle include calcium-channel blockers (p.1154) and nitrates (p.1155), as well as drugs with less well defined mecha- nisms of action such as papaverine (p.2191).
